actions.label: Message Earth
actions.desc: Power -5. Earth replies next sol: +5 to your lowest resource

calm.title: A calm sol
calm.text: Nothing unusual today. The panels soak up a little extra sunlight.
calm.fact: A sol (a Mars day) lasts about 24.6 hours, a little longer than an Earth day.

dust_storm.title: Dust storm!
dust_storm.text: Dust covers the sky and blocks the sunlight. Power drops.
dust_storm.fact: In the 2018 dust storm, the Opportunity rover's solar power fell from about 700 to 123 watt-hours in one sol.

solar_flare.title: Solar flare warning
solar_flare.text: The Sun threw out a burst of radiation. A strong shield protects the crew (damage is halved if Shield is 50 or more).
solar_flare.fact: NASA's DONKI database records solar flares and coronal mass ejections so teams can warn crews.

cold_night.title: Freezing night
cold_night.text: The heaters work extra hard tonight.
cold_night.fact: Mars temperatures can swing from about -89 C to -31 C.

earth_contact.title: Call from Earth
earth_contact.text: Mission control sends encouragement and a small supply boost.
earth_contact.fact: A radio message takes 3 to 22 minutes to travel one way between Mars and Earth.

radiation_day.title: Radiation check
radiation_day.text: Sensors show the usual background radiation. Keep the shield up.
radiation_day.fact: Curiosity measured about 0.64 millisieverts of radiation per day on the Mars surface.
radiation_day.source: Curiosity RAD instrument, Hassler et al., Science 2014
